The SDK binds Microsoft authentication to a session, so the catalog comes from the setup session's `rpc.model.list()`, not the global token-based API. The runtime cannot resolve managed settings for a Microsoft account yet, so the host applies none to that account's catalog; do not read policy from the setup session to compensate.

+The launch plan carries the selected Microsoft account beside its GitHub credentials, and the launcher follows the plan rather than the current selection. A new Microsoft conversation is created fully configured like any other and then signed in on that same SDK session through the current Entra authority, because the SDK accepts no Microsoft credential when opening a session; one that cannot be signed in is deleted. A resume the runtime accepts opens the session once and never logs in, so it keeps the sign-in the runtime saved. As for any account, only a resume the runtime rejects for lack of history falls back to a new session under the same ID, which is created and signed in like any new conversation. Conversation policy uses the runtime's normal global `client.rpc.managedSettings.resolve` call with the plan's GitHub token (absent for Microsoft), independently of the catalog omission. Explicitly scoped GitHub credentials keep their existing path; Microsoft automation readiness remains unavailable.

+The shared sign-in dialog offers Microsoft immediately when the M365 setting is enabled; otherwise it retains the existing Microsoft/EMU probe and sign-in path. An explicit Microsoft click authenticates the advertised discovery resource, waits for service publication, and authenticates only the chosen still-offered service. While discovery runs it answers the host's challenges for Microsoft resources once they are advertised (the challenge notification precedes the resource), prompting at most once per resource; a requirement that ordinary credential forwarding satisfies before setup has asked anything is not a failed attempt, so choosing that service acquires its credential the ordinary way; a permission that cannot be obtained for one service is not a setup failure, because the host's discovery result decides, and a requirement the host is still asking for is never treated as a service it offers. One offered service needs no chooser; cancellation retains Microsoft sign-in without completing setup. Missing services, rejected credentials and disconnected hosts never imply readiness or lack of entitlement. GitHub and GitHub Enterprise keep their ordinary sign-in paths; resource declarations do not supply account-menu or billing facts.

Copilot Connectors use the SDK session's GitHub credentials, including refreshable token providers. At create and resume, `CopilotSessionLauncher` checks `sessionAccountSelection`, obtains the opaque account ID from `session.rpc.connectors.getAccount()`, and reconciles that account without enumerating global accounts or matching tokens. Unsupported runtimes and unavailable accounts are logged and skip Connector reconciliation without preventing ordinary chat.
